_doc: The application's vocabulary: curated relation / namespace definitions, the salient-relation profiles and the is-a spines. Read by the platform's lexicon generator (python scripts/gen_lexicon.py), which writes them as the pack named `pack`; the schema is the platform specification's 'Lexicon declaration'.

relations.sys:related_to: related to — a general association between the two concepts.
relations.bench:references: references — the source bench binds the target Source pool/stream as reference material (never a copy).
relations.bench:about: about — the source hypothesis is about the target atom.
relations.bench:evidence_for: evidence for — the source evidence supports/contradicts/contextualises the target hypothesis.
relations.bench:cites: cites — the source (evidence/proof) cites the target atom or passage.
relations.bench:proves: proves — the source proof addresses the target hypothesis.
relations.bench:refers_to: refers to — the source bench note refers to the target atom.
relations.bench:trained_on: trained on — the source learned-model identity was trained on the target frozen train sample (the auditable data frame; the split is deterministic and recorded, never a hidden filter).
relations.bench:promoted_as: promoted as — the source learned-model identity is promoted as the target vlab observer, so its predictions become auditable observations like any reference observer's.
relations.bench:metrics_of: metrics of — the source metrics atom (accuracy / macro-F1 / per-class table / confusion, one aggregate) reports the target learned model on a held-out frozen frame.
relations.bench:evaluated_on: evaluated on — the source metrics atom was computed on the target frozen sample (the held-out test frame), so the score is tied to the exact auditable data it was measured on.
relations.bench:compares: compares — the source observe.diff aggregate atom compares the target observation run (before/after): observe.diff (T7) links its one summary atom bench:compares → both run atoms, so the Source Viewer shows the change without re-running the macro.
relations.bench:trained_in: trained in — the source learned-model identity was produced in the target dispatched execution (the B4 exec record on the world axis): which run produced this model is one link.
relations.sys:hit_via: hit via — the source access event arrived through the target referrer (pulse analytics acquisition; reserved).
relations.clab:frames: frames — the source question frames the target inquiry / criterion / tension.
relations.clab:observes: observes — the source agent/instrument observes the target occurrence.
relations.clab:reports: reports — the source agent reports the target observation.
relations.clab:reported_by: reported by — the source observation was reported by the target agent.
relations.clab:selects_as_example: selects as example — the source observation/case is selected as the target example.
relations.clab:exemplifies: exemplifies — the source example exemplifies the target concept/pattern.
relations.clab:supports: supports — the source is evidence in favour of the target claim/hypothesis/example.
relations.clab:challenges: challenges — the source is evidence against or a challenge to the target.
relations.clab:contradicts: contradicts — the source directly contradicts the target.
relations.clab:constrains: constrains — the source constrains the admissible readings of the target.
relations.clab:interprets_as: interprets as — the source interpretation reads the target as something.
relations.clab:interpreted_as: interpreted as — the source observation is interpreted as the target.
relations.clab:explains: explains — the source hypothesis explains the target.
relations.clab:presupposes: presupposes — the source presupposes the target.
relations.clab:depends_on: depends on — the source depends on the target (evidential/structural dependence).
relations.clab:uses: uses — the source agent/instrument uses the target apparatus.
relations.clab:measured_by: measured by — the source observation is measured by the target instrument.
relations.clab:replicated_by: replicated by — the source result is replicated by the target.
relations.clab:implies: implies — the source implies the target.
relations.clab:generalizes: generalizes — the source generalizes the target.
relations.clab:instantiates: instantiates — the source instantiates the target problem/pattern.
relations.clab:distinguishes: distinguishes — the source distinguishes the target cases.
relations.clab:contrasts_with: contrasts with — the source is set in contrast with the target.
relations.clab:bridges: bridges — the source bridge connects the target regions.
relations.clab:between: between — the source tension holds between the target endpoints.
relations.clab:reframes: reframes — the source reframes the target.
relations.clab:emerges_from: emerges from — the source concept emerges from the target precursors.
relations.clab:derived_from: derived from — the source example is derived from the target observation/structure.
relations.clab:illustrates: illustrates — the source example illustrates the target problem.
relations.clab:part_of_example: part of example — the source observation is part of the target example.
relations.clab:stabilizes_as: stabilizes as — the source pattern stabilizes as the target concept.
relations.clab:revises: revises — the source revises the target.
relations.clab:supersedes: supersedes — the source supersedes the target.
relations.clab:coexists_with: coexists with — the source coexists with the target without resolution.
relations.clab:evaluates: evaluates — the source assessment evaluates the target under a criterion.
relations.clab:proposes: proposes — the source agent proposes the target.
relations.clab:accepted_by: accepted by — the source proposal is accepted by the target agent.
relations.clab:disputed_by: disputed by — the source is disputed by the target agent.
relations.clab:sourced_by: sourced by — the source research operand is sourced by the target citation (provenance link carrying a locator).
relations.clab:cites: cites — the source citation cites the target research Source (bibliographic operand).
relations.responsible:approve: approve — the target agent must approve the named workflow step in the source society before it may advance (a gated step's approver; responsible:approve:<step>).
relations.responsible:exec: exec — the target agent holds execution rights for the named workflow step in the source society (responsible:exec:<step>).
relations.responsible:proposer: proposer — the target agent is responsible for putting forward proposals/hypotheses in the source research society (open workflow responsible).
relations.responsible:critic: critic — the target agent is responsible for challenging claims in the source research society (open workflow responsible).
relations.responsible:source_reviewer: source reviewer — the target agent is responsible for provenance/citation review in the source research society (open workflow responsible).
relations.responsible:ontology_editor: ontology editor — the target agent is responsible for the ontology-promotion boundary in the source research society (open workflow responsible).
relations.clab:contains: contains — the source (master thesis / neighborhood) contains the target (hypothesis / family) as a structural member.
relations.clab:about: about — the source hypothesis is about the target concept/question.
relations.clab:supported_by: supported by — the source hypothesis is supported by the target cluster/evidence.
relations.clab:challenged_by: challenged by — the source hypothesis is challenged by the target cluster/evidence.
relations.clab:leads_to: leads to — the source hypothesis leads to the target hypothesis/conclusion in a trajectory.
relations.clab:evaluated_by: evaluated by — the source master thesis is evaluated by the target conclusion.
relations.clab:key_proof: key proof — the source key-proof judgement designates the target cluster as decisive (a research judgement, not intrinsic; agents may disagree).
relations.clab:decisively_supports: decisively supports — the source key proof decisively supports the target hypothesis/thesis.
relations.clab:turning_point: turning point — the source turning-point judgement marks the target cluster as redirecting the trajectory against a hypothesis/thesis.
relations.clab:concludes_about: concludes about — the source conclusion evaluates the target hypothesis/master thesis (polarity affirm/negate/mixed/undetermined).
relations.clab:competes_with: competes with — the source conclusion competes with the target conclusion (multiple conclusions may coexist; non-destructive).
relations.clab:belongs_to_family: belongs to family — the source concept/cluster belongs to the target theoretical family.
relations.clab:family_next: family next — the source theoretical family transitions to the target family along a trajectory (initial → intermediate → destination).
relations.radu:in_source: in source — the source annotation passage belongs to the target source document (Radu Annotation model, source ≠ annotation).
relations.radu:annotates: annotates — the source annotation item (thesis/argument/definition/…) reads the target source passage; a reading of the document, not a property of it (Radu Annotation model, faithful source fidelity).
relations.radu:in_interpretation: in interpretation — the source annotation item belongs to the target Radu interpretation (the annotation is one annotator's reading; the same source may carry other interpretations).
relations.radu:orbits: orbits — the source thesis/argument/definition orbits the target central concept (Radu's dark-blue oval the annotation elements orbit; preserved with that role and nothing more).
relations.radu:in_module: in module — the source annotation item is grouped into the target module (Radu organizes elements into modules; the module boundary may itself be unresolved).
relations.radu:connected_to: connected to — the source annotation item is connected to the target item as Radu drew it; an intentionally NEUTRAL relation whose semantic type stays unresolved unless Radu explicitly supplied it (never inferred to supports/contradicts/defines/causes).
relations.delib:projects: projects — the source stance aggregation is projected into the target concept-labo deliberation field.
relations.delib:deliberates: deliberates — the source concept-labo deliberation field is posted into the target society for deliberation.
relations.delib:in_language: in language — the source feedback/response is written in the target language (its original locale; the response atom holds the primary-source original).
relations.delib:translates: translates — the source English machine-translation projects (translates) the target original-language response; a secondary, provenance=inferred atom kept traceable so translation artifacts can be distinguished from real disagreement.
relations.delib:source: source — the source response derives from the target original FULL-TEXT record (原票): the complete submission imported as a first-class, provenance=external atom and used as the analysis target (deeper than the feed comment); traceable via clab.trace.
relations.delib:mapped_stance: mapped stance — the source coded-answer response carries the target DECLARED stance token, assigned by an inspectable coded-field→stance mapping rule (never read from the text by the lexicon; never fabricated).
relations.delib:mapped_by: mapped by — the source response's stance was declared by the target first-class mapping-rule atom (the exact, versioned coded-answer→stance reading), so every mapped stance is traceable to the rule that made it.
relations.@discusses: discusses — the source text-stratum (a stylometry locus) treats the target real-world subject: a herb, formula, or doctrinal concept (the cross-laboratory non-textual layer; lets a passage be read against the materia medica it actually names).
relations.obs:of: observation of — the source telemetry observation is one timestamped sample about the target stable subject (the change lives in the observation, never in the subject's identity).
relations.obs:from: observation from — the source telemetry observation was delivered by the target live feed (provenance of a dynamic fact).
relations.obs:at: observation at — the source telemetry observation is located in the target geo cell (the shared substrate the feeds are crossed on).
relations.feed:tracks: tracks — the source live feed is currently tracking the target subject (an event / quake / satellite it is streaming observations about).
relations.@aligns_locus: aligns locus — the source alignment atom binds the target locus to a counterpart in another witness/recension or work (an explicit locus-to-locus correspondence that survives divergent chapter/section numbering, e.g. Pali book III to Chinese chapter 2); the substrate for crossing a lens across the corpus.
relations.sys:source: source — the target is a source or origin of the source atom.
relations.sys:abbreviation_of: abbreviation of — the source is a short form of the target.
relations.sys:capital_of: capital of — the source city is the capital of the target place.
relations.sys:has_capital: has capital — the target city is the capital of the source place.
relations.thesaurus:hypernym: hypernym — the target is a broader category of the source (is-a upward).
relations.thesaurus:hyponym: hyponym — the target is a narrower kind of the source (is-a downward).
relations.thesaurus:synonym: synonym — the two words share the same sense.
relations.thesaurus:external_ref: external reference — links the concept to an external record or resource.
relations.thesaurus:near_synonym: near synonym — the two words are close in sense without being interchangeable; weaker than `thesaurus:synonym` and asserted where a shade of difference matters.
relations.thesaurus:example_usage: example usage — the target is an attested use of the source concept: a sentence, a citation or a phrase showing the word at work rather than defining it.
relations.thesaurus:affective: affective — the target names the emotional colour the source concept carries. A relation about connotation rather than denotation, which is why it is not `thesaurus:related`.
relations.calc:has_emotion: has emotion — the source evokes or carries the target emotion.
relations.has_emotion: has emotion — the source evokes or carries the target emotion.
relations.media:depicts: depicts — the media atom depicts the target subject.
relations.media:video: video — links the atom to a video resource.
relations.geo:instance_of: instance of — the place is an instance of the target place type.
relations.geo:member_of: member of — the place is a member of the target grouping.
relations.geo:in_country: in country — the place lies within the target country.
relations.geo:borders: borders — the place shares a border with the target place.
relations.geo:official_language: official language — the target language is official in the place.
relations.home:located_in: located in — the item is normally located in the target room or zone.
relations.home:used_for: used for — the item is used for the target purpose.
relations.home:has_room: has room — the dwelling contains the target room.
relations.home:adjacent_to: adjacent to — the room adjoins the target room.
relations.home:zone: zone — the item belongs to the target home zone.
relations.rec:sweetness: sweetness — perceived sugar intensity on a 0-10 scale.
relations.rec:acidity: acidity — perceived sourness / acid intensity on a 0-10 scale.
relations.rec:heat: heat — perceived pungency / chilli heat on a 0-10 scale.
relations.rec:color: colour — the characteristic colour of the ingredient.
relations.bio:allergen: allergen — marks a substance as a biological allergy trigger.
relations.bio:dietflag: diet flag — a dietary classification flag for the food.
relations.bio:plant_part: plant part — the edible or used part of the plant.
relations.bio:climate: climate — the climate in which the organism grows.
relations.bio:source: source — the biological source the food is derived from.
relations.bio:source_primary: primary source — the main biological source of the food.
relations.bio:flesh_type: flesh type — the type of flesh (e.g. white / red / oily).
relations.bio:habitat: habitat — the natural habitat of the organism.
relations.bio:fruit_type: fruit type — the botanical fruit type (e.g. pome, drupe, berry).
relations.bio:herb_type: herb type — the culinary / botanical herb type.
relations.bio:nut_type: nut type — the botanical nut type.
relations.bio:legume_type: legume type — the botanical legume type.
relations.bio:grain_type: grain type — the cereal / grain type.
relations.bio:fat_source: fat source — the source of dietary fat.
relations.bio:husbandry: husbandry — the animal husbandry or rearing method.
relations.verb:acts_on: acts on — the verb acts on the target object.
relations.chrono:before: before — the source precedes the target in time.
relations.in_season: in season — the ingredient is in season during the target period.
relations.nutrition:glycemic: glycaemic level — the food's glycaemic index band.
relations.nutrition:fodmap: FODMAP level — the food's FODMAP fermentability band.
relations.diet:emphasized_in: emphasised in — the food is emphasised in the target diet.
relations.diet:excludes: excludes — the diet excludes the target food.
relations.diet:limited_in: limited in — the food is limited in the target diet.
relations.allergen:excludes: excludes allergen — the item excludes the target allergen.
relations.dietlaw:forbids: forbids — the dietary law forbids the target food.
relations.culinary:technique_type: technique type — the cooking technique class used.
relations.culinary:region: region — the culinary region of origin.
relations.culinary:component: component — a culinary component of the dish.
relations.culinary:cut_type: cut type — the butchery / knife cut type.
relations.culinary:condiment_type: condiment type — the class of condiment.
relations.culinary:use: culinary use — the typical culinary use of the ingredient.
relations.culinary:heat_level: heat level — the cooking heat level.
relations.culinary:common: commonly used with — a common culinary pairing.
relations.occasion:served_at: served at — the dish is served at the target occasion.
relations.cuisine:signature: signature dish — a signature dish of the cuisine.
relations.cuisine:staple: staple — a staple food of the cuisine.
relations.person:worked_in: worked in — the person worked in the target field or place.
relations.person:active_in: active in — the person was active in the target field or era.
relations.person:lived_in: lived in — the person lived in the target place.
relations.person:from_country: from country — the person's country of origin.
relations.person:belongs_to_school: belongs to school — the person belongs to the target school of thought.
relations.person:related_to: related to — a relation between the two people.
relations.people:flourished_in: flourished in — the person flourished in the target era or place.
relations.people:related_to: related to — a relation between the two people.
relations.deity:worshipped_in: worshipped in — the deity was worshipped in the target culture or place.
relations.deity:embodies: embodies — the deity embodies the target domain or quality.
relations.religion:branch_of: branch of — the tradition is a branch of the target religion.
relations.religion:originated_in: originated in — the religion originated in the target place.
relations.religion:sacred_to: sacred to — the item is sacred to the target religion.
relations.hist:territory_now: territory now — the historical territory now corresponds to the target place.
relations.hist:flourished_in: flourished in — the polity or culture flourished in the target era.
relations.hist:period_of: period of — the event belongs to the target historical period.
relations.hist:occurred_in: occurred in — the event occurred in the target place or time.
relations.hist:era_of: era of — the era of the target polity or culture.
relations.hist:concurrent_with: concurrent with — the two entities were concurrent in time.
relations.knowledge:in_branch: in branch — the concept sits in the target branch of knowledge.
relations.crosscut:manifests_in: manifests in — the cross-cutting theme manifests in the target field.
relations.dh:bridges: bridges — the digital-humanities method bridges the two fields.
relations.dh:area: area — the digital-humanities area of the work.
relations.dh:serves: serves — the method serves the target scholarly purpose.
relations.dh:grounded_in: grounded in — the method is grounded in the target discipline.
relations.dh:can_analyse: can analyse — the method can analyse the target material.
relations.sci_hist:achieved_in: achieved in — the scientific achievement was made in the target era.
relations.sci_hist:discovered_by: discovered by — the discovery was made by the target person.
relations.art:influenced_by: influenced by — the artist or movement was influenced by the target.
relations.art:derived_from: derived from — the style derives from the target.
relations.art:of_period: of period — the work belongs to the target art period.
relations.art:reacts_against: reacts against — the movement reacts against the target.
relations.art:preceded_by: preceded by — the movement was preceded by the target.
relations.arch:influenced_by: influenced by — the architectural style was influenced by the target.
relations.arch:derived_from: derived from — the architectural style derives from the target.
relations.arch:reacts_against: reacts against — the architectural style reacts against the target.
relations.law:influenced_by: influenced by — the legal tradition was influenced by the target.
relations.law:codified_in: codified in — the law was codified in the target code or era.
relations.law:contrasts_with: contrasts with — the legal concept contrasts with the target.
relations.law:derived_from: derived from — the law derives from the target source.
relations.law:source_of: source of — the source is a source of the target law.
relations.econ:field: field — the economics sub-field of the concept.
relations.labo:has_source: labo has source — the labo binds (references) the target Source Pool/Snapshot/Set as its Source projection; the resource is not owned.
relations.labo:has_concept: labo has concept — the labo binds the target concept / clab field as its Concept projection.
relations.labo:has_society: labo has society — the labo binds the target Society as an observer/operator of its namespace (never an owner).
relations.labo:in_labo: labo in labo — the source resource/interpretation belongs to the target labo namespace.
relations.labo:interpretation_of: labo interpretation of — the source interpretation is a (plural) reading of the target source atom/set/concept; the target may carry competing readings.
relations.labo:competes_with: labo competes with — the two interpretations are competing/contradictory readings of the same target (kept side by side, never collapsed).
relations.hyperlabo:composes: hyperlabo composes — the hyper labo references the target participating labo without merging or rewriting it.
relations.hyperlabo:joint_society: hyperlabo joint society — the hyper labo's Joint Research Task Force Society (in addition to, not instead of, the local Societies).
relations.hyperlabo:bridges: hyperlabo bridges — the cross-lab bridge connects the target local concept; it does NOT assert equivalence between local concepts.
relations.hyperlabo:in: hyperlabo in — the source bridge/chunk belongs to the target hyper labo namespace (cross-lab findings stay here until locally adopted).
relations.research:in_labo: research in labo — the Research Chunk / Publication Set belongs to the target labo's notebook.
relations.research:concerns: research concerns — the Research Chunk concerns the target concept / link / set.
relations.research:produced_by: research produced by — the Research Chunk was produced by the target workflow / experiment / analysis run.
relations.research:assessed_by: research assessed by — the Research Chunk was assessed by the target Society / role.
relations.research:supports: research supports — the source Research Chunk supports the target chunk/claim.
relations.research:contradicts: research contradicts — the source Research Chunk contradicts the target chunk/claim.
relations.research:supersedes: research supersedes — the source Research Chunk supersedes the target (the superseded chunk is retained, never deleted).
relations.research:follows: research follows — the source Research Chunk follows the target in the research sequence.
relations.research:refines: research refines — the source Research Chunk refines the target.
relations.research:publishes: research publishes — the Publication Set includes the target Research Chunk (a curated recomposition, backlinked).
relations.research:in_publication: research in publication — the Research Chunk is included in the target Publication Set (backlink).
relations.analysis:in_labo: analysis in labo — the analysis run belongs to the target labo.
relations.analysis:input: analysis input — the analysis run took the target Set as input.
relations.analysis:uses_plugin: analysis uses plugin — the analysis run used the target (replaceable) plugin.
relations.analysis:produces: analysis produces — the analysis run produced the target result Set / projection (an output, not a truth).
relations.analysis:derived_from: analysis derived from — the source result Set (algebra/core/boundary) was derived from the target source Sets.
relations.vis:observes: observes — the source machine OBSERVATION (or detection) observes the target artwork Source Atom. A machine observation is never an artwork property: the observer, model version, and confidence stay attached, and the Source Atom is never mutated.
relations.vis:observer: observer — the source observation was produced by the target immutable model identity (family/variant/version/weights/thresholds). A new model or config is a new observation, never an overwrite.
relations.vis:in_run: in run — the source observation belongs to the target vision run (the reproducible experiment execution that recorded it).
relations.vis:compares: compares — the source model-comparison record compares the two target observations (the difference between observers is first-class research data, not noise).
relations.vis:embedding_ref: embedding ref — the source feature observation references the target stored embedding (large vectors live in the tensor store, never inlined in the atom).
relations.vis:derived_from: derived from — the source derived feature observation (e.g. the lightweight Color⊕Geometry⊕Texture vector) is assembled from the target originating observation; the originating observations are never erased (an analytical derivative, not a source fact).

namespaces.vis: vis — Visual Curation Laboratory relations (machine vision): vis:observes / vis:observer / vis:in_run / vis:compares / vis:embedding_ref bind observations to artworks, models, runs, and comparisons.
namespaces.vlab: vlab — the Visual Curation Laboratory's own registry atoms; vlab:learned:<id> registers a learned classifier head (promoted from a learning bench) as an observer whose predictions are auditable observations.
namespaces.vision_run: vision_run — a reproducible machine-observation experiment execution over a source pool (vision_run:<id>): the observer configs, model versions, thresholds, software versions, timings, and success/failure counts. Re-running mints a new run; previous runs stay intact.
namespaces.delib: delib — the deliberation bridge: operators that flow a survey of collected public feedback through stance aggregation into a concept-labo field and on into a society (delib:projects, delib:deliberates, delib:in_language, delib:translates).
namespaces.language: language — a natural language a source is written in (ISO 639-1); language:<code> names one. Used to keep the original locale of public feedback as the primary source (一次資料), with English as a secondary translation-projection.
namespaces.feed: feed — a registered live-telemetry source (its schedule + field mapping); feed:<id> auto-fetches public keyless data every interval and maps it to observation atoms.
namespaces.entity: entity — a STABLE telemetry subject tracked by a feed (an event, a quake, a satellite); entity:<feed>:<extid> is content-addressed by (feed, external id) so its identity never changes as its observations stream in.
namespaces.obs: obs — a telemetry OBSERVATION: one timestamped, geo-located sample about a subject; obs:<entity>:<bucket> is content-addressed by (subject, time-bucket) so re-fetches are idempotent. provenance=telemetry (fenced from learning).
namespaces.gen: gen — the Genealogy model (where traditions come from): a corpus as ordered loci measured through many discipline lenses (textual strata, chronology, concept, tradition, materials, attestation, geography), boundaries overlaid as corroboration vs held divergence, with a cross-work source-stemma. The superset of the stylometry (sty) model.
namespaces.sty: sty — the Stylometry model, a single-lens SUBSET of Genealogy (gen): one text as ordered loci, a feature×locus matrix, its discontinuities read as composition seams.
namespaces.topic: topic — an EU policy topic (one of the Commission's 38 areas) that a consultation sits under.
namespaces.initiative: initiative — an EU legislative initiative: the proposal a public consultation gathers feedback on.
namespaces.consultation: consultation — a public consultation / feedback round under an initiative (its framing question).
namespaces.stakeholder: stakeholder — a submitter to a consultation: a category (stakeholder:type:*) or a named organisation.
namespaces.media: media — media resources (images, video) and what they depict.
namespaces.score: score — numeric scores attached via typed link (0-1 or scaled).
namespaces.home: home — the everyday home: rooms, zones, household items.
namespaces.food: food — the food domain (ingredients, dishes, cuisines).
namespaces.culinary: culinary — culinary techniques, cuts, components and uses.
namespaces.yoga: yoga — Yoga: the darshana as practice (Patanjali's eight limbs, prana, koshas).
namespaces.samkhya: samkhya — Samkhya metaphysics: prakriti/purusha, the five great elements (mahabhuta).
namespaces.guna: guna — the three gunas (sattva, rajas, tamas): the qualitative axis of Samkhya, Yoga, and Ayurveda.
namespaces.verb: verb — verbs and the objects they act on.
namespaces.people: people — people and their flourishing eras.
namespaces.deity: deity — deities and the domains they embody.
namespaces.hist: hist — historical polities, periods and events.
namespaces.art: art — visual art movements and works.
namespaces.dietlaw: dietlaw — religious and cultural dietary laws.
namespaces.occasion: occasion — occasions and events food is served at.
namespaces.ext: ext — external routes and resource links (provenance atoms).
namespaces.wp: wp — Wikipedia external identity (alias wp:<Title> → en.wikipedia.org exit link).
namespaces.wd: wd — Wikidata external identity (alias wd:<Qid> → wikidata.org exit link).
namespaces.clab: clab — Concept-Laboratory / Nebula model namespace: the epistemic relations (clab:supports, clab:interprets_as, clab:bridges, …) and operand markers for thought-experiment fields.
namespaces.radu: radu — Radu Annotation model namespace: a Concept-Laboratory DERIVED model that faithfully reconstructs Radu Tulai's annotation method (thesis/argument/definition/notion/module/concept/connection) as one annotator's reading of a source, preserving his terms and leaving genuine gaps unresolved.
namespaces.shelf: shelf — The Thinker's Shelf reading-programme namespace: the vocabulary a read work is opened with — the source decomposition (book/edition/page/section/passage/bibliographical entry/person/work/place/language/printer/historical reference), the four strata (original/structural/analytical/commentary), the four interpretation levels (SOURCE/DERIVED/INTERPRETIVE/SPECULATIVE), the society roles (Reader/Listener/Commentator), the reading-cycle steps, and the relations the semantic bridge runs on. BOOK OPENETH BOOK: a book is opened, never summarised.
namespaces.hyperlabo: hyperlabo — an interdisciplinary composition namespace that references multiple Labos without merging or rewriting them; hyperlabo:<name> adds a cross-lab namespace + a Joint Research Task Force Society.
namespaces.research: research — Research Notebook units: research:chunk:* (the cronon-ordered history — question/hypothesis/experiment/observation/finding/decision/…, failed/superseded states retained) and research:publication_set:* (selected/reordered chunks recomposed into a paper).
namespaces.analysis: analysis — the Analysis View provenance layer over the Source Window: analysis:run:* (input Set + plugin/version + params + cronon), analysis:set:* (result Sets — clustering output as Sets, never the one true classification), analysis:projection:* (a rendered projection).
namespaces.plugin: plugin — an installed analysis/transform plugin referenced by an analysis run (plugin:<name>); the numerical engine is replaceable, the GUI is only a projection/control surface over it.
namespaces.station: station — Akasha broadcasting-station namespace. (a) The guest-readable program guide (番組表): station:studios / station:studio:<gid> / station:shows:<gid> / station:show:<gid>:<space>, which society.station renders across studios (categories) and their shows. (b) The PROGRAMME STATE vocabulary a registered programme is always in, one atom each, joined to set:station:state:<state> at mint: station:state:warming_up (registered, its boot airing queued), station:state:on_air (a turn aired inside the live window), station:state:rebroadcast (the last airing repeated until the next lands — no model call, no reservation, no new observation or atom), station:state:standing_by (registered and not playing, always with a reason). (c) The skip/standby REASONS: station:reason:fresh (the last airing is younger than the interval, so a redeploy neither airs nor spends twice), station:reason:llm_pool (admission could not hold the reservation), station:reason:provider_429 (the provider rate-limited the call), station:reason:budget_calls (AKASHA'S OWN daily call ceiling is spent — llm.budget calls=), station:reason:budget_tokens (AKASHA'S OWN token ceiling for the day or month is spent — the MONEY bound, since cost is per token), station:reason:waiting_source (a declared source is not frozen yet), station:reason:runs_per_day (the programme's own declared runs for today are spent), station:reason:breaker (consecutive failures — a research bench drops to manual, a STATION programme stays armed and keeps trying, because a broadcaster removing itself from the schedule is the silence the ruling forbids), station:reason:not_provisioned (a runtime PRECONDITION is missing — the cycle is not on the bench; the cure is a boot, which reconciles, never a retry), station:reason:no_text (the model answered with nothing usable). The three refusal families are kept APART on purpose: llm_pool is the shared pool, provider_429 is the provider, budget_* are this cell's own ceilings — reading one for the other sends an operator to the wrong place. A value the code compares against is vocabulary: the code uses these ids, never a free string, and `unclassified` stays reserved for a value that does not exist — which a registered programme's cells never are.
